notes.title: "Mojika - Truth Rears Its Ugly Head" is now available!
notes.notes:
[h1] [b]I Know Your Ugliness[/b][/h1]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2697560

The international version of "Mojika - Truth Rears Its Ugly Head" developed by NitroOrigin and published by JAST has now been launched on STEAM! The achievement system is supported (there is a conflict with the patch). There is a 10% discount for the initial release (for one week)!

[img]https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2697560/extras/mojika_image_05.gif?t=1743433723[/img]

This work has its script written by Shimokura Vio (whose representative works include "Your Love Story with Her and Her", "Tokyo Necro", and "STEINS; GATE") and its original art created by Hamashima Shigeo (whose representative works include "euphoria" and "Yua Club").

[img]https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2697560/extras/mojika_image_03.gif?t=1743433723[/img]

[h3]Story Overview[/h3]
Suteru is an outcast burdened by his ugly appearance who possesses a rare and unsettling gift called “Wordsight” in which thoughts materialize as words. His unique ability allows him to uncover the disturbing secrets of those who torment him and help him seek revenge.

[img]https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2697560/extras/mojika_image_04.gif?t=1743433723[/img]

[h3]Known Possible Problems and Solutions:[/h3]
1. Crashing when fast-forwarding
- If you fast-forward too much, it may get stuck when using “Wordsight”. Just restart the game.

2. Infinite loop when fast-forwarding the plot in the broadcasting room
- Please cancel the fast-forward and click to proceed with the plot.

3. Black screen of the "Word Curse" during the plot in Hanatsubaki Shin'in
- Please cancel the fast-forward and click to proceed with the plot.

4. c++ error message appears before the True Ending
- Please restart the game and load the save file.

5. No response after starting the game
- There may be such a situation when starting the launcher for the first time. Please wait patiently for the launcher to appear.

If you have any other questions, it is recommended to consult through the official social media or the customer service email to get a quicker response.
Thank you for your support!

notes.title: Notice on Potential Misclassification of Steam Screenshots
notes.notes:
Due to Valve's official request for developers concerning the review of adult content in the community, we will be systematically organizing content within the Steam community to continue providing an enhanced gaming experience for more players on this platform.

Given the high volume of manual reviews, there may be instances of normal content being mistakenly flagged.

We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this operation may have caused. If you believe your content has been incorrectly flagged, please submit a ticket on our official website, including the ID of the screenshot that was mistakenly flagged. 
We will relay this information to the relevant management personnel for further verification and handling.

notes.title: Tokyo Necro Releases 03 / 13 / 23!
notes.notes:
In a cyberpunk dystopia, Tokyo is frozen over and riddled with the undead, and it falls to the members of a Living Dead Stalker Agency to do the dirty work of cleaning up the streets.

Tokyo Necro, brought to you by Nitro Origin (formerly Nitroplus), the same developers behind Song of Saya, is the latest and greatest in action visual novels. Gorgeous art transitions into 3D models during fully animated fight scenes, making this one of the most graphically intensive visual novels ever made. And those graphics aren't just for show either, underpinning a gripping narrative set within an incredibly vivid locale.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2183070/Tokyo_Necro

notes.title: How a comic tried to reimagine cult visual novel Song Of Saya
notes.notes:
A Panel Shaped Screen is a monthly column where Giada Zavarise explores how comics and videogames inspire each other. This month, Giada examines the differences between cult horror visual novel Song Of Saya and its American comic adaptation.

Seeing Song Of Saya (Saya no Uta) featured on Steam is like finding a dead body on the shore.
It’s a terrific visual novel, this one, but one always recommended in whispers. A horror love story festooned in blood and gore, and with a list of content warnings longer than my games backlog. It can be completed in a single sitting, but will haunt you for years. Its presence on a mainstream storefront feels viscerally wrong, like something dark and rotten that should not have been brought to light.

And yet, this is not the first time Song Of Saya got introduced to a bigger audience. Because a decade ago, it got an American comic adaptation.

notes.title: Deeply messed-up visual novel Saya no Uta is coming to Steam
notes.notes:
Steam's doors have been open to a lot of adult games it previously wouldn't have sold, but it's still a surprise to see Saya no Uta ~ Song of Saya appear in the list of upcoming games. This is a visual novel infamous because, as Brittany Vincent put it, "Not only are there descriptions of gratuitous violence, but sexual assault, adult scenes featuring a young-looking female character, and various other bits of awfulness are sprinkled throughout."

And yet it's enduringly popular. Brittany went on to write that "despite all its horrific content (and in many cases because of it, including some of the grotesque fates that befall certain characters), Saya no Uta remains one of my most-played visual novels."

It's the story of a young man who survives a car crash but is permanently changed, perceiving the world as as a hellscape of gore and people as monsters. Even his friends look demonic. Only a young girl named Saya appears normal, but when his senses tell him everything mundane is monstrous what does it mean that she seems innocent?

Saya no Uta is an effective work of horror written by Gen Urobuchi (of Psycho-Pass, Fate/Zero, and Madoka Magica fame), but it's let down by some out-of-place hentai scenes that feel like they were inserted because it was was released by Nitroplus, and that's what they're known for. The kind of dudes who call everyone else "normies" think these scenes are essential, but for the rest of us they're out of place.

Saya no Uta will be available on Steam from August 12, remastered in a new engine with higher quality image resolution, and promises improved translation and better system compatibility with Windows 10. We'll have to wait and see if the story's also been altered.
